bib.title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

question: Can a pretraining objective keep autoregressive likelihood (no input corruption, no independence assumption) while still learning bidirectional context, and does that beat BERT's masked denoising?
hypothesis: Maximising expected likelihood over all factorization orders gives bidirectional context without BERT's [MASK] discrepancy and independence assumption, and so pretrains better.
contributions: Two-stream (content and query) self-attention for target-aware prediction
Integration of Transformer-XL segment recurrence and relative positional encodings, plus relative segment encodings
Outperforms BERT on 20 tasks under comparable settings

method.summary: XLNet pretrains a Transformer-XL with a permutation LM objective: sample a factorization order, predict only the last 1/K tokens in that order using attention masks (positions stay in natural order) and a query stream that sees position but not content. XLNet-Large matches BERT-Large size and is trained on 32.89B tokens of mixed corpora; ablations use BERT-Base-sized models on Wikipedia+Books.
method.task: self-supervised pretraining (permutation language modeling), then finetuning on NLU tasks

limits: Parameter count is never given; XLNet-Large is only said to be 'a similar model size' to BERT-Large.
Ablation (Table 6) reports medians of 5 runs without variance; several gaps (SST-2, NSP rows) are within a point.
Table 1 compares against the best of 3 BERT variants; the permutation objective is not isolated from the Transformer-XL backbone except by the DAE+Transformer-XL row at BERT-Base scale.
Large-scale win over RoBERTa uses different data than the fair comparison, and XLNet is slightly lower than RoBERTa on GLUE RTE dev.
The ablation compares to BERT only at Base size; no ablation of partial prediction K beyond 6 vs 7, and pretraining data effects for XLNet-Large are not separated from objective.
Model still underfit at the end of 500K steps. SQuAD1.1 test result is from an older model version.
The claim that the permutation objective mostly improves data efficiency is conjecture backed only by qualitative attention analysis.
